title: Frontend: Price Range Slider
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Price Range Slider. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Two range inputs Minimum and Maximum, names min/max, are bounded 0..100 and initially 0/100. Editing min clamps it <= max; max clamps it >= min. Display min-max in [data-testid="range"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep one valid range and normalize each change against bounds and the other endpoint.
alternativeApproaches: Support currency-specific step sizes without floating-point drift in accepted prices.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Equal endpoints; min above max; keyboard arrows.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
